offers.name: ASUS Vivobook 15 15.6" 60Hz Laptop - Intel Core 5 320 - 8GB RAM - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 Home - Quiet Blue

reviews.quote: The Vivobook 15 cuts a few corners to keep its cost down and the display is dull, but its performance is right up there with laptops that cost a couple thousand bucks more.
An inexpensive laptop that performs well — good performance and comfort under heavy loads, comfortable keyboard, and cooling that quietly does its job.

praises: $649.99 sale price is one of the cheapest ways into a modern 6-core x86 with an NVMe SSD
8GB sits in a standard DDR5 SO-DIMM — a $25 stick later and it is a 16GB machine
Same solid Core 5 320 CPU as the pricier twin; everyday Windows feels quick
Webcam privacy shutter and numeric keypad retained from the 16GB SKU
Light 1.7 kg for a 15.6" with numpad; easy carry for a student
complaints: 8GB in 2026 Windows 11 is tight out of the box — Chrome-heavy users feel it within weeks
250-nit washed-out panel is the same dim compromise as the twin SKU
USB-C is data-only: no PD charging, no external monitor over USB-C
Deck and lid flex; hinge wobble typical of this chassis
Regular $1,099.99 is hard to justify when the 16GB twin sells for $849.99

standouts: Cheapest entry into the upgradable-DDR5 Vivobook 15 chassis at its $649.99 sale
design_philosophy: The volume tier of ASUS's budget 15.6" line: identical chassis and CPU as the 16GB SKU with RAM trimmed to hit a deeper sale price. It is explicitly a start-now-upgrade-later machine — the single DDR5 SO-DIMM invites a cheap RAM bump, which is exactly why it beats the soldered-RAM rivals at $649.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the 16GB Vivobook 15 twin (same chassis/panel/CPU): -0.6 productivity for 8GB out-of-box, +0.5 upgradability (RAM bump is the intended path and cheap). No pro review exists for the line (see SHARED-vivobook.md). Battery estimated from ~42 Wh 3-cell. Image URL best-guess BBY CDN pattern.
